study.title: Alterations in neuroplasticity and functional connectivity of striatal subregions in Bell's palsy patients after acupuncture
study.study_design: Longitudinal within-subject resting-state fMRI study; pre-treatment and post-treatment scans in Bell's palsy patients receiving acupuncture
study.population: Patients with Bell's palsy (acute unilateral facial paralysis), disease course less than 14 days, no prior treatment, H-B scores IV-VI
study.disease_condition: Bell's palsy (acute unilateral facial paralysis caused by inflammation of the facial nerve)
study.inclusion_criteria: BP diagnosed by two experienced physicians using the House-Brackmann (H-B) score; disease course of Bell's palsy of less than 14 days; had not received any treatment; H-B scores IV ~ VI
study.exclusion_criteria: History of physical or mental disorders; head motion exceeding 3 mm (imaging exclusion)

arms.dropouts: 5 patients did not complete the second scan; another 5 were excluded due to head motion exceeding 3 mm

conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI scan before any acupuncture treatment

conditions.timepoint_exact: last day of the 4-week treatment, 15 min following withdrawal of needles
conditions.scan_context: Resting-state fMRI scan immediately after final acupuncture session (15 min following needle withdrawal)

interventions.stimulation_type: manual acupuncture with deqi elicitation at bilateral LI4
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: ipsilateral facial points and bilateral LI4
interventions.laterality_exact: ipsilateral facial acupoints and bilateral Hegu (LI4)
interventions.needle_type_exact: Disposable acupuncture needles; Jaichen, Jianshu, China
interventions.penetration_exact: GB14, EX-HN4, and EX-HN5 were inserted horizontally; BL2, LI20, ST6, ST7, ST4, SI18, and LI4 were inserted perpendicularly
interventions.manipulation_exact: After insertion at bilateral LI4, manual stimulation (lifting-thrusting and twirling) was applied to elicit the characteristic 'deqi' sensation. Needle manipulation was standardized across sessions to ensure consistency of stimulation intensity.
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: yes; deqi sensation described as numbness, distention, or heaviness was elicited at bilateral LI4
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: 4 treatment sessions per week for 4 consecutive weeks, 16 sessions in total
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: senior chief physician with over 30 years of clinical experience specializing in the treatment of facial palsy

sensory_interoceptive_responses.item_or_subscale_exact: deqi sensation (numbness, distention, or heaviness) at bilateral LI4
sensory_interoceptive_responses.value_exact: sensation typically described by patients as numbness, distention, or heaviness
sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Deqi was described narratively as a target sensation at LI4; no quantitative deqi scale was used

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: T1-weighted structural images using MP-RAGE sequence; echo-planar T2*-weighted images (EPIs) for functional resting state
neuroimaging_methods.TR_exact: functional: TR = 2000 ms; structural: TR = 1900 ms
neuroimaging_methods.TE_exact: functional: TE = 30 ms; structural: TE = 2.45 ms
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 200 time points of functional resting state data
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM8), Welcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, University College, London, UK
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: CONN toolbox v15.g; SPM8; MATLAB (MathWorks, Inc., Natick, MA)
neuroimaging_methods.coordinate_space_reported_exact: MNI (referred to as 'NMI coordinates' and 'MNI coordinates (mm)' in the paper)
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: Band-pass filtering in a frequency window of 0.008-0.09 Hz (for ReHo); fALFF calculated on preprocessed data without band-pass filtering to quantify relative power of spontaneous low-frequency (0.01-0.08 Hz) oscillations
statistical_thresholds_exact: GRF corrected with a voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 and a cluster-level threshold of p < 0.05 (for whole-brain ReHo/fALFF and seed-based FC analyses)
FDR q < 0.05 (for 12×12 seed-to-seed functional connectivity analysis)
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Gaussian random field (GRF) theory with voxel-level threshold of p < 0.001 and cluster-level threshold of p < 0.05; false discovery rate (FDR, q < 0.05) for seed-to-seed analysis

extraction_notes.note: The paper reports 'NMI coordinates' (likely MNI) and 'MNI coordinates (mm)' inconsistently across text and tables. All coordinates have been extracted as MNI based on table headers in Table 2 and Table 3.

The paper uses 'I' (ipsilateral) and 'C' (contralateral) to refer to the affected and unaffected sides after image flipping. A right-left flipping procedure was applied to left-sided palsy images, so 'ipsilateral' consistently means the affected side across participants.

In Table 3, the contrast header is 'Post>Pre' but many peak z scores are negative (e.g., -5.16, -4.65, -4.28, -4.78, -4.99, -4.78, -5.34). The paper's text states these reflect 'decreased connectivity' post-treatment. The positive entry for DC_C (z = 6.22) and the pattern described in text as 'enhanced internal connectivity' may reflect a display convention or mixed directionality within the single table. This inconsistency is flagged for human review.

The correlation analyses (Section 3.4) use combined pre- and post-treatment data points from 20 participants (n = 40 total observations), as FC values were extracted from both timepoints and correlated with corresponding HB scores. The paper states 'For each subject, FC values were extracted from brain regions that showed significant changes in the group-level FC analysis.' The exact number of observations per correlation is not explicitly stated; the n_analyzed fields for correlation contrasts are listed as 40 (20 subjects × 2 timepoints) as an inference.

The n_analyzed for correlation analyses is inferred. The paper states FC values from both pre- and post-treatment scans were correlated with corresponding HB scores, implying n = 40 (20 subjects × 2 timepoints), but this is not explicitly confirmed.
No adverse events were reported in the paper. Adverse event reporting is absent from the methods and results sections.

Expectancy, blinding success, credibility, and allocation guessing measures were not reported. The study had no sham or control group, so these measures are not applicable in the conventional sense, but expectancy was not assessed.
Needle retention time per session is not reported. Only the number of sessions (16 over 4 weeks) and session frequency (4 per week) are stated.
The cluster extent unit (voxels vs. mm3) is not explicitly stated in Table 2 or Table 3. 'Cluster size' values have been extracted as reported without unit interpretation.

The paper refers to 'Postcentral_L(aaL)' in Table 2 for the fALFF result, but also to 'contralateral postcentral gyrus' in the text. After flipping, 'contralateral' refers to the unaffected side. The exact atlas abbreviation '(aaL)' is unclear from the PDF.

The internal striatal connectivity results (12×12 seed-to-seed analysis, Figure 2) are presented primarily in figures. Individual edge statistics (exact z-scores, p-values for each connection) are not provided in a table; only the directional summary is extractable.

DRP_C is listed as 'NO' in Table 3, indicating no significant results. VRP_C, VRP_I, VSi_C, VSi_I, VSs_C, VSs_I are also listed as 'NO'. These null results have been noted but not extracted as separate contrast entries.

The paper states 'the second MRI scan was performed on the last day of the 4-week treatment, 15 min following withdrawal of needles.' This indicates the post-treatment scan was performed immediately after the final session, capturing acute post-acupuncture neural effects in addition to treatment-period changes.
No healthy control group was included in this study. All comparisons are within-subject (pre vs. post-treatment) within the single Bell's palsy patient group.
